aesthetic: Archiv — a paper-white Swiss typographic system where cold phosphor and cautionary amber surface only as semantic markers against an unwavering warm ground, the grid itself carrying all expressive weight
chromaticArc: Slides 1–12 hold pure warm paper (#F8F5F0) throughout the framing and context sections; three chapter-break slides shift to warm stone (#EDE8E0) with ink-black type for structural punctuation; cold phosphor teal surfaces only on the Geist/philosophical slides (2–3 instances) as a ghost-pale overprint trace; cautionary amber emerges in the critical and prophetic closing sequence (slides 30–38), the palette arc moving from paper-white intellectual calm toward a muted terminal warmth without ever breaking into darkness.
gridStrategy: Title-only slides anchor text to col 6 span 26 row 10–16, leaving the right third and bottom quarter as measured silence; body slides run a primary zone col 4 span 36 with generous top margin; dialectical slides (consolidation vs. open-source, pros vs. cons) split into two narrow columns col 4 span 24 and col 34 span 22 that approach but never resolve; tabular assessment slides use a strict three-column grid col 4/22/40 for Müller-Brockmann modular precision.

fontStrategy.secondarySlides: No secondary font — all typographic registers are achieved through size (12–36px), tracking (0em on titles to 0.15em on labels), and weight (400 regular throughout) within Helvetica Neue alone

accentStrategy: The sole structural accent is a 0.5px hairline rule in ink-black used once per chapter-break slide as a horizontal separator at the grid baseline; on philosophical slides a cold phosphor tint (#5BBFB5 at 15% opacity) washes the text zone only, producing the ghost-pale overprint effect without introducing a decorative element — no icons, bars, or ornaments appear anywhere in the deck.
